headline: KRX Activates Sell-Side Sidecar For KOSPI Following Sharp Decline
seoTitle: (URGENT) Bourse operator activates sell-side sidecar for…
metaDescription: The Korea Exchange suspended program trading for the KOSPI index after a significant market decline, following a buy-side trigger the previous day.
aiSummaryBullets: The Korea Exchange implemented a sell-side sidecar program to curb volatility on the KOSPI.
The measure was triggered following a rapid decline in market share prices.
This follows a buy-side sidecar activation that occurred the previous day during a market surge.
aiContextParagraph: The Korea Exchange (KRX) serves as the primary securities exchange operator in South Korea, managing the KOSPI index. Trading regulations include sidecar mechanisms, which are designed to mitigate market instability by temporarily suspending program trading for a period of five minutes when the index experiences sudden, sharp fluctuations in value. On November 25, 2026, the bourse operator activated a sell-side sidecar in response to a notable drop in the KOSPI index. This development occurred shortly after the exchange had triggered a buy-side sidecar on November 24, 2026, during a period of significant market gains. These rapid consecutive activations reflect a recent stretch of high volatility for the Korean equity market, requiring intervention by market authorities to maintain order and manage rapid price movements in domestic share prices.
whyItIsViral: The event is being tracked by two independent news outlets following consecutive days of triggered market volatility measures.
